parsed.why: No trans-specific offence; same-sex lawful; identity checks no documented targeting of visitors. No facility bans or custody-by-birth-sex record. Weakness: no statutory LGR, only implicit constitutional cover, dated reports of everyday discrimination. No documented recourse for trans-specific hate.

Cross-dressing expressly criminalised (Art. 152), a universal exposure for any outable visitor; sodomy penalties up to life; documented state extrajudicial killings and torture of LGBTQ people; no LGR; vigilante targeting. Severe tier-1 plus tier-2 state threat.

Decriminalised, no gender-identity offence, incitement and hate-aggravator provisions, documented broadly neutral social attitudes and an activist record of no community-targeted violence. Deductions: no LGR, no operative discrimination remedy, repealed employment protection, thin trans-specific data.

Documented state pattern: mass street detentions of trans women for ID checks (313 violations, 299 detentions), prison placement by birth sex with a custody death, strip searches, hostile ministerial rhetoric and a draft criminalising LGBT people. Tier-1 and tier-2 exposures; no working remedy.

No criminalisation and gender identity named in national anti-discrimination law plus entity hate-crime enhancements; but organised mob violence at Pride/festivals with a court finding police failed to protect, police-cancelled screenings, and hostile survey attitudes. Thin recourse beyond paper.
